facts.function: Medial wall of the ankle mortise; attachment of deltoid ligament and flexor retinaculum
facts.attachments: Lateral surface articulates with medial facet of talus; tibialis posterior/FDL tendons groove behind it

facts.function: Proximal fibula: lateral knee landmark; common fibular nerve winds round the neck
Palpable at posterolateral knee
facts.attachments: Articulates with lateral tibial condyle; biceps femoris and fibular collateral ligament insert

facts.function: Common fibular nerve wraps around it: fracture/cast compression → foot drop
facts.attachments: Narrow segment just below head; fibularis longus arises nearby

facts.function: Lateral wall of ankle mortise; lower and more posterior than medial malleolus
facts.attachments: Articulates with lateral talus; ATFL, CFL, PTFL attach; fibularis tendons groove behind it

facts.function: Transmits body weight from tibia to foot; no muscle attachments; keystone of the medial arch
facts.attachments: Trochlea with tibia/malleoli; head with navicular; inferior facets with calcaneus (subtalar joint)
facts.supply: Blood enters mainly via neck (retrograde) → neck fracture risks avascular necrosis of body

facts.function: Rounded anterior end; keystone of medial arch
facts.attachments: Articulates with navicular; supported from below by spring ligament

facts.function: Common fracture site (forced dorsiflexion) → risk of avascular necrosis of body
facts.supply: Main entry of talar blood supply

facts.function: Bulk of talus carrying trochlea; posterior process grooved by FHL tendon
facts.attachments: Inferior facet with calcaneus (subtalar joint)

facts.function: Superior articular surface of talocrural joint; wider anteriorly → ankle most stable in dorsiflexion
facts.attachments: Articulates with tibial plafond and both malleoli

facts.function: Heel bone: largest tarsal, posterior pillar of both longitudinal arches
facts.attachments: Tuberosity: calcaneal tendon, plantar aponeurosis, AH/FDB/ADM; sustentaculum tali supports talus

facts.function: Tuberosity = main insertion of tibialis posterior; palpable medial foot landmark
facts.attachments: Navicular articulates with talar head and three cuneiforms; spring ligament attaches to plantar surface

facts.function: Keystone of the lateral longitudinal arch
facts.attachments: Articulates with calcaneus, lateral cuneiform, MT4–5; plantar groove for fibularis longus tendon

facts.function: Three wedge-shaped tarsals forming the transverse arch between navicular and MT1–3
Largest cuneiform; part of medial column
facts.attachments: Articulates with navicular and MT1; tibialis anterior and fibularis longus insert

facts.function: Smallest cuneiform; recessed, locking the MT2 base (Lisfranc stability)
facts.attachments: Articulates with navicular and base of MT2

facts.function: Wedge between intermediate cuneiform and cuboid
facts.attachments: Articulates with navicular, cuboid and base of MT3

facts.function: Five long bones of the forefoot; heads bear weight at push-off
Shortest, thickest; head bears two sesamoids and much push-off load
facts.attachments: Base: tibialis anterior and fibularis longus insert

facts.function: Longest; base keyed between cuneiforms; common stress (march) fracture site
facts.attachments: Base tied to medial cuneiform by Lisfranc ligament

facts.function: Central ray; stress fractures also common
facts.attachments: Base articulates with lateral cuneiform

facts.function: Part of lateral column
facts.attachments: Base articulates with cuboid

facts.function: Lateral column; tuberosity avulsion or Jones (proximal diaphysis) fractures
facts.attachments: Tuberosity: fibularis brevis; dorsal base: fibularis tertius

facts.function: 14 per foot: hallux has 2, other toes 3; levers for toe flexion and extension
Base articulates with metatarsal head (MTP joint)
facts.attachments: Insertions of EHB, AH, FHB, adductor hallucis, interossei

facts.function: Toes II–V only (hallux has none)
facts.attachments: Insertion of flexor digitorum brevis

facts.function: Terminal phalanges supporting the toenails
facts.attachments: Insertions of FDL (II–V), FHL and EHL (hallux)

facts.function: Dorsiflexes and inverts foot
facts.attachments: Lateral tibial condyle/shaft, interosseous membrane → medial cuneiform, base of MT1

facts.function: Extends great toe; dorsiflexes foot
facts.attachments: Middle anterior fibula, interosseous membrane → base of distal phalanx of hallux

facts.function: Extends lateral four toes; dorsiflexes foot
facts.attachments: Lateral tibial condyle, anterior fibula, interosseous membrane → middle/distal phalanges II–V via extensor expansions

facts.function: Dorsiflexes and everts foot
facts.attachments: Distal anterior fibula → dorsum of base of MT5

facts.function: Everts and plantarflexes foot; supports lateral and transverse arches
facts.attachments: Head and upper lateral fibula → medial cuneiform, base of MT1 (crosses sole in cuboid groove)

facts.function: Everts foot; weak plantarflexion
facts.attachments: Lower lateral fibula → tuberosity of base of MT5

facts.function: Plantarflexes foot at ankle; flexes knee
facts.attachments: Medial and lateral femoral condyles → calcaneal tuberosity via calcaneal tendon

facts.function: Plantarflexes foot; postural muscle; calf venous pump
facts.attachments: Posterior fibular head/upper fibula, soleal line of tibia → calcaneal tuberosity via calcaneal tendon
facts.supply: Popliteal, posterior tibial and fibular arteries

facts.function: Transmits triceps surae (gastrocnemius + soleus) pull for plantarflexion; ankle jerk reflex (S1–S2); rupture → weak push-off
facts.attachments: Gastrocnemius + soleus → middle of posterior calcaneal tuberosity

facts.function: Unlocks the extended knee (laterally rotates femur on fixed tibia)
facts.attachments: Lateral femoral condyle, lateral meniscus → posterior tibia above soleal line

facts.function: Inverts and plantarflexes foot; main dynamic support of medial longitudinal arch
facts.attachments: Interosseous membrane, posterior tibia/fibula → navicular tuberosity, cuneiforms, cuboid, bases MT2–4

facts.function: Flexes lateral four toes; plantarflexes and inverts foot
facts.attachments: Posterior tibia below soleal line → bases of distal phalanges II–V

facts.function: Flexes great toe (push-off); plantarflexes foot; supports medial arch
facts.attachments: Lower posterior fibula, interosseous membrane → base of distal phalanx of hallux

facts.function: Strong medial collateral ligament; resists eversion (may avulse medial malleolus rather than tear)
facts.attachments: Medial malleolus → navicular, talar neck, sustentaculum tali, posterior talus (four parts)

facts.function: Resists anterior talar shift and inversion in plantarflexion; most commonly sprained ankle ligament
facts.attachments: Anterior margin of lateral malleolus → lateral neck of talus

facts.function: Resists inversion with ankle in neutral; second ligament torn in inversion sprains
facts.attachments: Tip of lateral malleolus → lateral surface of calcaneus

facts.function: Strongest lateral ankle ligament; resists posterior talar shift; rarely torn
facts.attachments: Malleolar fossa of fibula → lateral tubercle of posterior talar process

facts.function: Longitudinal arches distribute body weight and absorb shock in stance and gait
Higher, mobile, shock-absorbing arch; talar head is keystone
facts.attachments: Calcaneus, talus, navicular, cuneiforms, MT1–3; held by spring ligament, tibialis posterior, plantar aponeurosis

facts.function: Low, rigid, weight-bearing arch; cuboid is keystone
facts.attachments: Calcaneus, cuboid, MT4–5; held by long/short plantar ligaments and fibularis longus

facts.function: Side-to-side arch across cuneiforms, cuboid and metatarsal bases
facts.attachments: Supported by fibularis longus tendon, tibialis posterior and transverse head of adductor hallucis

facts.function: Supports longitudinal arches (windlass mechanism), protects sole; inflamed at heel origin in plantar fasciitis
facts.attachments: Medial process of calcaneal tuberosity → five digital slips to toe flexor sheaths

facts.function: Supports head of talus; key passive support of medial longitudinal arch (laxity → flatfoot)
facts.attachments: Sustentaculum tali → plantar surface of navicular

facts.function: Plantar calcaneocuboid ligaments supporting the lateral longitudinal arch
Supports lateral arch; turns cuboid groove into tunnel for fibularis longus
facts.attachments: Plantar calcaneus → cuboid ridge and bases of MT2–4

facts.function: Plantar calcaneocuboid ligament; supports lateral arch, deep to long plantar ligament
facts.attachments: Anterior tubercle of calcaneus → plantar cuboid

facts.function: Roofs tarsal tunnel; holds deep posterior compartment tendons in place behind medial malleolus
facts.attachments: Medial malleolus → medial surface of calcaneus

facts.function: Transmits tibialis posterior, FDL, posterior tibial vessels, tibial nerve, FHL; nerve compression → tarsal tunnel syndrome
facts.attachments: Between flexor retinaculum and medial talus/calcaneus, behind medial malleolus

facts.function: Extends toes II–IV (assists EDL)
facts.attachments: Superolateral calcaneus → long extensor tendons of toes II–IV

facts.function: Extends great toe at MTP joint
facts.attachments: Superolateral calcaneus → base of proximal phalanx of hallux

facts.function: Abducts and flexes great toe; supports medial arch
facts.attachments: Medial process of calcaneal tuberosity, flexor retinaculum → medial base of proximal phalanx of hallux

facts.function: Flexes great toe at MTP joint
facts.attachments: Plantar cuboid, lateral cuneiform → both sides of base of proximal phalanx of hallux (sesamoids in tendons)

facts.function: Flexes lateral four toes at PIP joints
facts.attachments: Medial process of calcaneal tuberosity, plantar aponeurosis → sides of middle phalanges II–V

facts.function: Straightens oblique pull of FDL tendons; assists toe flexion
facts.attachments: Medial and lateral plantar calcaneus → posterolateral margin of FDL tendon

facts.function: Flex MTP and extend IP joints of toes II–V
facts.innervation: 1st: medial plantar nerve; 2nd–4th: lateral plantar nerve (S2–S3)
facts.attachments: FDL tendons → medial sides of extensor expansions of toes II–V

facts.function: Abducts and flexes little toe
facts.attachments: Medial and lateral processes of calcaneal tuberosity → lateral base of proximal phalanx of toe V

facts.function: Flexes little toe at MTP joint
facts.attachments: Base of MT5 → base of proximal phalanx of toe V

facts.function: Adducts great toe; transverse head helps maintain transverse arch
facts.attachments: Oblique: bases MT2–4; transverse: plantar MTP ligaments III–V → lateral base of proximal phalanx of hallux

facts.function: Abduct (dorsal) and adduct (plantar) toes relative to 2nd toe; flex MTP, extend IP joints
Abduct toes II–IV from axis of 2nd toe (DAB); four bipennate
facts.attachments: Adjacent sides of MT1–5 → bases of proximal phalanges II–IV (2nd toe gets two)

facts.function: Adduct toes III–V toward 2nd toe (PAD); three unipennate
facts.attachments: Medial sides of MT3–5 → medial bases of proximal phalanges III–V

facts.function: Adduct toes III–V toward 2nd toe (PAD); flex MTP joints
facts.attachments: Medial sides of MT3–5 → medial bases of proximal phalanges III–V

facts.function: Motor to anterior + lateral compartments (via deep/superficial branches); injury at fibular neck → foot drop, steppage gait
facts.attachments: Sciatic → along biceps femoris in popliteal fossa → round fibular neck → deep + superficial fibular nerves

facts.function: Motor: anterior compartment, EDB/EHB (dorsiflexion, toe extension); sensory: first web space
facts.attachments: Common fibular → interosseous membrane with anterior tibial artery → lateral to dorsalis pedis → first web space

facts.function: Motor: fibularis longus and brevis (eversion); sensory: most of dorsum of foot, distal anterolateral leg
facts.attachments: Common fibular → lateral compartment → pierces deep fascia distal leg → medial and intermediate dorsal cutaneous nerves

facts.function: Motor: posterior leg compartment and sole (via plantar nerves); sensory: sole and heel; injury → no plantarflexion, toe flexion
facts.attachments: Sciatic → popliteal fossa (most superficial) → deep to soleus with posterior tibial artery → tarsal tunnel → plantar nerves

facts.function: Terminal branches of tibial nerve (in tarsal tunnel) supplying intrinsic sole muscles and plantar skin
Like median nerve in hand: AH, FDB, FHB, 1st lumbrical; skin of medial sole and 3½ toes
facts.attachments: Tibial nerve → between abductor hallucis and FDB with medial plantar artery

facts.function: Like ulnar nerve: QP, ADM, FDMB, adductor hallucis, interossei, lumbricals 2–4; skin of lateral 1½ toes
facts.attachments: Tibial nerve → between FDB and QP → superficial and deep (with plantar arch) branches

facts.function: Sensory only: skin of medial leg and medial foot; at risk in great saphenous vein harvest/cutdown
facts.innervation: L3–L4; cutaneous terminal branch of femoral nerve
facts.attachments: Adductor canal → medial knee → with great saphenous vein → anterior to medial malleolus

facts.function: Sensory: posterolateral distal leg, lateral foot and little toe; common nerve biopsy/graft donor
facts.innervation: S1–S2; medial sural cutaneous (tibial) + sural communicating (common fibular)
facts.attachments: With small saphenous vein down calf → behind lateral malleolus → lateral border of foot

facts.function: Diamond behind knee containing popliteal artery (deepest), vein, tibial and common fibular nerves, popliteal nodes
facts.attachments: Biceps femoris (superolateral), semimembranosus/semitendinosus (superomedial), gastrocnemius heads (inferior); floor femur, capsule, popliteus

facts.function: Supplies knee (genicular arteries) and leg; deepest structure in popliteal fossa; common site of peripheral aneurysm
facts.attachments: Femoral artery at adductor hiatus → lower border of popliteus → anterior + posterior tibial arteries

facts.function: Supplies anterior compartment of leg
facts.attachments: Popliteal → above interosseous membrane into anterior compartment, with deep fibular nerve → dorsalis pedis at ankle

facts.function: Supplies posterior compartment and sole; pulse behind medial malleolus
facts.attachments: Popliteal → deep to soleus, gives fibular artery → tarsal tunnel → medial + lateral plantar arteries

facts.function: Supplies lateral and deep posterior compartments and fibula
facts.attachments: Posterior tibial (just below popliteus) → along fibula near FHL → lateral calcaneal branches

facts.function: Supplies dorsum of foot; pulse lateral to EHL tendon, over navicular/cuneiforms
facts.attachments: Continuation of anterior tibial at ankle → arcuate artery; deep plantar artery joins plantar arch

facts.function: Terminal branches of posterior tibial artery, arising deep to abductor hallucis, supplying the sole
Smaller branch; supplies medial sole and hallux
facts.attachments: Posterior tibial → between abductor hallucis and FDB → digital branches

facts.function: Larger branch; supplies lateral sole and forms the deep plantar arch
facts.attachments: Posterior tibial → obliquely laterally between FDB and QP → plantar arch

facts.function: Supplies toes via plantar metatarsal and digital arteries
facts.attachments: Continuation of lateral plantar artery across MT bases → joins deep plantar branch of dorsalis pedis

facts.function: Paired deep veins (venae comitantes) draining leg compartments to popliteal vein; common site of DVT
Drain anterior compartment and dorsum of foot
facts.attachments: Accompany anterior tibial artery → join posterior tibial veins → popliteal vein

facts.function: Drain posterior compartment and sole; receive fibular veins
facts.attachments: Accompany posterior tibial artery → popliteal vein

facts.function: Drains leg and knee; receives small saphenous vein; DVT site
facts.attachments: Union of tibial veins at popliteus → superficial to popliteal artery → femoral vein at adductor hiatus

facts.function: Main superficial vein of medial limb; harvested for CABG; cutdown anterior to medial malleolus
facts.attachments: Medial end of dorsal venous arch → anterior to medial malleolus → medial leg/thigh → femoral vein at saphenous opening

facts.function: Superficial drainage of lateral foot and posterior calf
facts.attachments: Lateral end of dorsal venous arch → behind lateral malleolus with sural nerve → popliteal vein

facts.function: Collects dorsal digital and metatarsal veins of the foot
facts.attachments: Across dorsum of metatarsals; medial end → great saphenous, lateral end → small saphenous vein
